==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|stripe}}, {{m|enm|strype}}, from {{der|en|dum|-}} or {{der|en|gml|strîpe}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*strīpā}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*strīpō}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*strīpô}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|Striepe|t=stripe, strip}}, {{cog|fy|stripe|t=stripe}}, {{cog|nl|streep|t=stripe}}, {{cog|nds-de|Striepe}}, {{m|nds-de|Striep}}, {{m|nds-de|Streep|t=stripe}}, {{cog|de|Streifen|t=stripe, strip, band}}, {{cog|da|stribe|t=stripe}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/stɹaɪp/|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/stɹaɪp/|a=GA,CA}} * {{audio|en|en-us-stripe.ogg|a=GA}} * {{audio|en|en-ca-stripe.ogg|a=Canada}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪp|s=1}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} [[file:Striped-Hyena.JPG|thumb|A striped hyena.]] # A [[long]] [[region]] of a single [[colour]] in a repeating pattern of similar regions. #: {{ux|en|zebra '''stripes'''}} # A long, relatively [[straight]] region against a different coloured background. #* '''8 Sep 2019''', Peter Conrad in ''{{w|The Guardian}}'', ''[https://www.theguardian.com/books/2019/sep/08/susan-sontag-her-life-benjamin-moser-review Sontag: Her Life by Benjamin Moser review – heavyweight study of a critical colossus]'' # {{lb|en|in the plural}} The [[badge]] worn by certain [[officer]]s in the [[military]] or other forces. # {{lb|en|informal}} Distinguishing characteristic; sign; likeness; sort. #: {{ux|en|''persons of the same political '''stripe'''''}} #: {{ux|en|a tyrant of a very different '''stripe'''}} #* '''20 May 2018''', Hadley Freeman in ''{{w|The Guardian}}'', ''[https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/may/20/is-meghan-markle-the-american-the-royals-needed-all-along Is Meghan Markle the American the royals have needed all along?]'' # A long, narrow [[mark]] left by [[strike|striking]] someone with a [[whip]] or [[stick]]; a [[blow]] or [[lash]] with a whip, stick, or [[scourge]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|I|2|passage=Thou most lying slave,
Whom '''stripes''' may move, not kindness!}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Deuteronomy|25|3||Forty '''stripes''' he [the judge] may give him [the wicked man], and not exceed:}} #* '''1735''', {{w|James Thomson (poet, born 1700)|James Thomson}}, ''The Four Seasons, and Other Poems,'' London: J. Millan and A. Millar, “Winter,” lines{{nbsp}}353-354, p.{{nbsp}}21,[http://name.umdl.umich.edu/004810089.0001.000] #* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage=Stones to eat and bitter water for their thirst, and '''stripes''' for tender nurture.}} # A [[slash]] cut into the [[flesh]] as a [[punishment]]. # {{lb|en|weaving}} A [[pattern]] produced by arranging the [[warp]] [[thread]]s in sets of alternating colours, or in sets presenting some other [[contrast]] of appearance. # {{senseid|en|pool}} Any of the [[ball]]s marked with stripes in the game of [[pool]], which one player aims to [[pot]], the other player taking the [[spot]]s. # {{lb|en|computing}} A portion of data distributed across several separate physical [[disk]]s for the sake of [[redundancy]]. # {{lb|en|motor racing|slang}} The start/finish line. ====Derived terms==== {{col3|en|title=Terms derived from ''stripe'' (noun)|bestriped|bluestripe|bootstripe|chalkstripe|destripe|goldstripe|headstripe|interstripe|magstripe|midstripe|multistripe|nanostripe|pinstripe|stripeless|stripelike|stripeseed|stripetail|stripewise|stripey|tigerstripe|hickory stripe|railroad stripe|sooty stripe|earn one's stripes|eyestripe|of the same stripe|show one's true stripes|striped|stripy|true stripes|charity stripe|eye-stripe|go-faster stripe|magnetic stripe|pleating to the stripe|stripe-breasted tit|stripe bamboo|tiger stripe|tiger of a different stripe|Árpád stripe|candy stripe|racer stripe|racing stripe}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|long straight region of a colour}} * Aramaic: * Bashkir: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * German: * Greek: * Hawaiian: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Hunsrik: * Indonesian: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Latin: * Latvian: * Lithuanian: * Malay: * Māori: * Naga: * Norwegian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Rarotongan: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|полоса́|f}}, {{t+|ru|поло́ска|f}} * Samoan: * Scottish Gaelic: * Serbo-Croatian: * Shor: * Slovak: * Southern Altai: * Spanish: * Swahili: * Swedish: * Tahitian: * Telugu: * Tongan: * Yiddish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|badge}} * Azerbaijani: * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * Greek: * Italian: * Latvian: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|наши́вка|f}}, {{t+|ru|шевро́н|m}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|a long narrow mark}} * Finnish: * Greek: * Māori: {{trans-bottom}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} #
